extracted.intended_audience: typographers, book designers, printers, and typesetters
extracted.subtask_description: A specimen sheet showing the same sample paragraph set in multiple typefaces, point sizes, and settings (leaded vs solid) to evaluate legibility, display treatment, and glyph coverage for book/press typesetting.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPECIMENS OF TYPES IN USE (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Page presents specimens of types in use by rendering the same sample passage (Polybius excerpt) repeatedly in different type families, point sizes, and settings so the reader can compare type appearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the repeated paragraph across sizes and families to judge overall legibility, color of the page (type density), and suitability of a face for body text or display. The heading 'SPECIMENS OF TYPES IN USE' frames the sheet as demonstrative rather than prescriptive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type family labels (MODERN / OLD STYLE / MONOTYPE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections are grouped under type-family headings such as 'MODERN', 'OLD STYLE', and 'MONOTYPE'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These labels identify the classification of the face being shown; compare faces within and between these families to assess stylistic appropriateness for the work (e.g., modern vs old-style characteristics). The page uses these exact family headings as selectors for evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point size and number notation (e.g. 'EIGHT POINT NO. FIFTY-SEVEN', 'SIX POINT NO. THIRTY-ONE', 'TWELVE POINT NO. EIGHT')
rubrics_metrics.description: Each specimen block is headed by an explicit size and catalogue number like 'SIX POINT NO. THIRTY-ONE', 'EIGHT POINT NO. THIRTY-ONE', 'ELEVEN POINT NO. EIGHT', 'TWELVE POINT NO. EIGHT', etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point size and the foundry/catalog number are presented to indicate exact sizing and cutting; evaluate type at intended sizes by comparing the same text set at these labeled sizes to judge readability, x-height, stroke contrast, and spacing at those exact points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leaded vs [Solid] setting indicator ('[Leaded]' or '[Solid]')
rubrics_metrics.description: Some specimen headings include a bracketed setting indicator such as '[Leaded]' or '[Solid]'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This marks whether additional leading (line spacing) is used or whether the text is set solid. Use the comparison to assess how leading affects readability and page color; prefer 'Leaded' for increased readability in dense text, 'Solid' for compact display settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display lines in uppercase for emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimens include occasional all-caps display lines (e.g. 'A WORLD-EMPIRE, INCLUDING ALL THE LANDS' or fully capitalized emphatic sentences) embedded in the samples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These display lines illustrate how the face behaves in uppercase or display use — check letterspacing, weight, and impact when set in caps for headings or emphatic passages. Observe whether caps remain legible and aesthetically appropriate at given sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a consistent sample paragraph (Polybius excerpt) for comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: The same paragraph about Polybius, Carthage, Alexander, etc., is repeatedly used as the sample text across specimens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using identical textual content across specimens makes differences attributable to the face/size/setting rather than content. When evaluating, focus on differences in word shapes, leading, measure, and word breaks produced by each specimen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of numerals, uppercase vowel clusters, and special glyph rows (e.g., '1234567890', 'AEIOU', assorted glyph strings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimen blocks include lines showing numerals '1234567890', vowel clusters 'AEIOU', miscellaneous letter groupings, and other glyph strings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These lines demonstrate numeral and caps design, spacing, and alignment; use them to verify glyph coverage, figure style (lining vs old-style), and behavior of particular letter combinations. They also reveal how the face treats punctuation and diacritics where present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printer/press identification and layout elements ('THE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO PRESS')
rubrics_metrics.description: The sheet includes the press name and pagination/layout elements (e.g., 'THE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO PRESS', page numbers, specimen index-like numbering).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies provenance and suggests intended application (book/academic press). Use the press label and layout cues to assess how the face and sizes integrate with house style and pagination practices; these elements demonstrate expected appearance in real printed matter.
